findings.title: Split the growing ready-state core
findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Split the growing ready-state core**

This addition grows `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs` from 998 raw / 889 rough lines to 1,077 raw / 961 rough lines, moving it into the repository watchlist's near-hard tier. The required recurring-review checklist says that a source file already past the 600-line cap must be split when a change grows it (`docs/pr-checklists/recurring-review-patterns.md:191-195`); since `scripts/` has no `max-lines` lint, CI will not enforce this automatically. Extract the CodeRabbit signal classification into a sibling module with meaningful headroom.

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.title: Trust only authorized closeout requests
findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Trust only authorized closeout requests**

On public pull requests, this loop accepts the marker from every issue commenter without checking the author or `author_association`. An outside user—or even a comment quoting the documented template—can therefore make the signal `requested`; the new babysit workflow then forbids the maintainer from posting the real closeout request for that head, potentially skipping the intended CodeRabbit review. Filter marker comments to trusted maintainers/agents before treating them as requests.

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.title: Authenticate closeout markers in the cloud loop
findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Authenticate closeout markers in the cloud loop**

When a public PR is babysat through the MCP fallback, this condition accepts the marker from any top-level commenter, unlike the new local classifier's maintainer/agent check. An outside user can quote the template for the current head, causing the cloud agent to suppress the real CodeRabbit closeout request and skip the intended review. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier comment is that this changed cloud workflow still directs agents to check only for marker presence; require an authorized association or recognized agent identity here too.
